title: teamLab to Open Digital Art Museum in US
paragraphs: teamLab, the Japanese art collective known for its immersive digital artworks, has announced plans to open its first permanent museum in the United States.

The museum, which was announced in late October 2026, will be built at OCVIBE, a new 100-acre district in Anaheim, Southern California, that is currently under construction. It is scheduled to open in 2030. With an area of about 110,000 square feet, the museum will feature artworks that respond to the presence of visitors, which is typical of teamLab's work. The building is being designed by the architecture firm smith-clementi, and it will have a largely windowless interior and an exterior that changes appearance with the light.

teamLab's founder, Toshiyuki Inoko, said that it was "with great joy" that the group was announcing its first major museum in North America. Meanwhile, Mike Waterman, the head of the tourism organization Visit Anaheim, described the project as "a powerful statement about where our destination is headed."

The museum will be part of a larger development funded by a $5 billion private investment from the Samueli family. When OCVIBE is completed in 2033, it is expected to include 20 acres of open space, walking trails, more than 2,000 homes, over 35 places to eat and three entertainment venues. The first stage, which includes a concert hall for 5,000 people, is due to open in 2027. Anaheim is already famous as the home of Disneyland, and local tourism leaders hope the museum will give visitors another reason to come.

Although the permanent museum is still years away, American fans can see teamLab's work sooner. An exhibition is being held at the Smart Museum of Art at the University of Chicago until February 2027.
